questions_for_audit: Which exact Rust native CLI profile and experimental successor profile are in the current roadmap denominator, and which are historical or advisory only?
For each advertised command, what is the full chain from public command parser to implementation, target bytes, verifier, and ledger consumer?
Which test expected outcomes are independently calculated versus emitted by the same evaluator/API used by the system under test?
Can Quint acceptance traces be mechanically serialized and replayed into Rust tests while preserving exact state, effects, and refusal atomicity?
Which K cases have a genuinely independent source of expected outputs, and which compare two projections sharing parser/compiler helpers?
For the current public CLI, do tests launch the installed or packed command as well as the source entrypoint?
Are beta and Rust test manifests path-safe under symlinks, Windows separators, malformed UTF-8, duplicate keys, unknown fields, and oversized nested inputs?
How are complete post-state, all financial effects, fees, refund gross accounting, liabilities, and rounding independently checked per profile?
What evidence connects source-static mapped-role compile artifacts to source semantics and authority checks, and what stops at local static compilation?
Which CI workflows gate source compiler/runtime changes versus documentation only, and do they exercise clean package installs?
Which distinct profiles have positive, negative, boundary, mutation, property-based, and cold-process tests today; which coverage cells remain unknown?
What is the accepted predicate and evidence format for every G01–G24 item, U0–U7, M1–M17 and MC/SP gate without merging incompatible denominators?
What would be required to show native signer, relation, circuit identity, network, Anchor and current state all bind to the exact source candidate?
How are dynamic dependencies, toolchain versions, generated artifacts, fixture oracles and retained receipts made reproducible in a clean checkout?
Which historical receipts belong to a different tree/profile and must stay scoped to their original candidate rather than current source?
What attacks distinguish missing account/history authentication from internally consistent local state simulation?
Where does code publish terminal distinctions between prepared, authenticated, proven, submitted, final, accepted and financially qualified states?
How will the audit classify tests that are merely specified, source-inspected, historically run, currently rerun, or externally accepted?
